title: Why a button can light a lamp
premise: A button sends a request to a controller, and the controller turns on a lamp.
context: Explain a two-step signal path rather than implying that a button powers the lamp.
signature: Pocket Cutouts: blunt plum ink contours, warm ivory paper, apricot focal shapes, teal shadows, simple rounded shapes and ample negative space. Expressive objects; no baked words.

cues.say: and then it switches the lamp on.
cues.caption: and then it switches the lamp on.
and then it switches the lamp on.

cues.say: The button doesn't power the lamp directly.
It tells the controller what to do.

panels.visual: One large round apricot push button on the far left, one rectangular teal controller box in the middle, and one tall desk lamp on the right. Isolated on ivory paper with lots of clear white space between all three. The lamp is fully DARK, no illumination, no glowing rays or beams. There are NO painted arrows, NO symbols, no signal lines, no connections between objects, no cables and no writing anywhere.
panels.keep: Left-to-right readable diagram, no other buttons, controllers or lamps.
